newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam calls for state secrets to be kept secret.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam calls for state secrets to be kept secret.

text.p: Vietnam's prime minister has called for a drive to keep state secrets out of the public domain following "serious" confidentiality lapses by public organisations, the Lao Dong newspaper said on Saturday.

The journal said Vo Van Kiet ordered ministries, government offices and People's Committees to tighten control over information and review what to keep under wraps and what to make public according to social and economic developments.
"The situation of revealing state secrets at some organs and in local areas is still serious," the state-controlled newspaper said, quoting Kiet's official order.
"At the same time, there is an abuse of regulations on the protection of state secrets..." it said.
State secrecy regulations cover a multitude of areas in communist Vietnam such as military activities, the movements of government officials and banking.
The government, faced with growing bad loan problems in the banking system, recently released a list of financial market topics which were to be barred or restricted from media coverage.
